h1:
Buriram in 3 Days, 2 Nights
City, Temples, Sport & Nature
intro: Buriram packs a lot of different things into one province: a sports city with a football stadium and a race circuit that host international events, thousand-year-old Khmer temples sitting on old volcanoes, and quiet countryside just outside town. With only a single day you usually get to pick just one of those. This 3-day, 2-night plan keeps day one in the city and tacks on Khao Kradong, heads south on day two for the Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam temples, then closes out day three with the race circuit and a bit of nature before you drive home. We've checked the opening hours and entry fees for everywhere in this plan.

blocks.html: Downtown Buriram is small and walkable — most restaurants and hotels sit within a few kilometres of each other. But the headline sights, like Phanom Rung, are nearly 80 km south of town, while the race circuit and Pela Plern are off in a different direction. Having your own car or a rental is by far the easiest way to get around. So we've set up day one as an easy day in the city, blocked out the whole of day two to head south for the temples, and saved the last day for stops at Chang Arena and a bit of nature before the drive back. If you're coming when Buriram United has a home match or during the MotoGP weekend in early March, book your accommodation well ahead — rooms fill up fast.

blocks.text: Day 1 — City walk, Khao Kradong, Chang Arena tour

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Check in downtown, climb Khao Kradong to pay respects, then tour Chang Arena

items.activity: Arrive in Buriram, check in at a downtown hotel or drop your bags first, then grab an easy breakfast around the city centre
items.note: If you arrive by train at Buriram station, the city centre is very close — you can walk or hop on a motorbike taxi. If you've driven, just park at your hotel.

items.activity: Lunch at Kwangchow, a long-running spot in town — order red pork and crispy pork over rice, congee, or pork blood soup
items.note: Open around 07:00–15:00. It gets busy late morning, so going before noon means little to no wait. Around 50–70 THB a plate.

items.activity: Drive up Khao Kradong Forest Park, an extinct old volcano — pay respects to the large Phra Suphatthara Bophit Buddha image at the top, then walk the suspension bridge to see the remains of the volcanic crater
items.note: Two ways up: the 297-step staircase, or drive to the summit. Free entry, about 6 km from town. From the top you get a full view across Buriram city.

items.activity: Head down from the hill to Chang Arena and buy a Stadium Tour ticket — a guide takes you into the players' dressing room and press room, up into the stands, and down to pitchside
items.note: The stadium tour runs roughly 09:00–17:00, costs around 100–150 THB, and takes about an hour. If you happen to be here on a Buriram United home-match day, buying a match ticket instead gives you the full atmosphere.

items.activity: Dinner at Kai Yang Sida, a grilled-chicken spot Buriram locals love that's been open more than 25 years, over on Anuwat Road — order the crispy-skin grilled chicken with som tam
items.note: Open daily around 09:00–21:00. Grilled chicken is 120–180 THB a bird; half a bird is plenty for two. It gets busy in the evening, so you may have to queue.

blocks.title: Day-one tips
blocks.html: Khao Kradong gets strong sun in the afternoon. If you drive to the summit you'll be fine, but if you want to climb the 297 steps for photos, skip the hottest part of midday. For the Chang Arena tour, if you're in a big group or bringing kids, check the tour time slots at the stadium first — some slots fill up.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Buriram trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.text: Day 2 — The Phanom Rung & Mueang Tam temple route

blocks.html: Today is the highlight of the trip. Phanom Rung sits in Chaloem Phra Kiat district, about 77 km from town — roughly an hour and a half by car. You'll want to leave early to beat the heat and fit both Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam into one day. The two temples are only about 8 km apart, so chaining them together is easy.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Phanom Rung on the volcano crater, then on to Mueang Tam

items.activity: Leave town early and drive south toward Chaloem Phra Kiat district — stop for breakfast along the way or pick something up to eat in the car
items.note: About 77 km, roughly an hour and a half. Leaving early gets you to Phanom Rung before the sun gets harsh.

items.activity: Walk up to Phanom Rung, a pink sandstone temple on top of an old volcano — cross the naga bridge and climb the long stairway to the central sanctuary, and see the famous Reclining Vishnu lintel
items.note: Open daily 06:00–18:00. Entry 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners, 30 THB to bring a car in. The path up is long and exposed, so bring a hat and water.

items.activity: Head down from Phanom Rung and drive on to Mueang Tam in Prakhon Chai district, about 8 km away — see the L-shaped ponds and the five-headed nagas ringing the baray
items.note: Open daily 06:00–18:00. Entry 20 THB for Thais. There's a discounted combined Phanom Rung + Mueang Tam ticket — ask at the ticket window.

items.activity: Lunch around Prakhon Chai — try kung jom or the local Isan dishes this district is known for
items.note: Prakhon Chai is famous for kung jom, a punchy local specialty. Local restaurants are inexpensive — about 60–120 THB per person.

items.activity: Drive back into town and stop at a café to rest your legs before dinner
items.note: The drive back takes about an hour and a half. If you're still up for it, you can stop at Wat Khao Angkhan, a temple on another old volcano along the way — but allow extra time.

items.activity: Dinner at Jay Hung Noodles, a well-known spot in town famous for its rich broth and bouncy meatballs
items.note: Open evenings, around 17:30–21:30. A bowl is 50–70 THB. There's a queue in the early evening, so going before six is easier.

blocks.title: Before you climb Phanom Rung
blocks.html: In April and again in September–October there's a phenomenon where the sun shines straight through all 15 of the temple's doorways — crowds are especially heavy then. If you're set on seeing it, go before dawn and allow for parking. On an ordinary weekday it's far quieter and much easier to walk and shoot photos.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Race circuit + nature before heading home

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Stop at Chang International Circuit, then Pela Plern before the drive home

items.activity: Check out of your hotel and have an easy breakfast in town before setting off
items.note: If you haven't picked up gifts yet, stop at a souvenir shop in town for Chinese sausage, mu yo (Vietnamese pork sausage), or local sweets first.

items.activity: Stop at Chang International Circuit, the race track that hosts MotoGP — take photos out front and browse the souvenir shop
items.note: When there's no race you can't go inside the track, but you can take photos from outside. Come in late February to early March and it lines up with MotoGP, which opens its season here — you'll need tickets and accommodation booked far ahead.

items.activity: Drive to Pela Plern, a boutique resort and adventure camp in Khu Mueang district — walk the botanical garden, the greenhouse, and the model village
items.note: Garden entry is about 150 THB per person; the water park is charged separately. Open daily, good for kids or nature photographers. Allow about 2–3 hours to walk it.

items.activity: Lunch at Pela Plern or a spot along the way, then get ready for the drive back
items.note: Khu Mueang is north of Buriram city, so on the way back you can either head into town or make for the highway out of the province, depending on your route.

items.activity: Set off home, avoiding the Sunday-evening rush when traffic out of Isan tends to be heavy
items.note: If you're not in a rush, stop at Hua Lamphong Noi, Sa-ra-krao Market, or the city's walking street on Friday–Saturday evenings before you go.

blocks.text: Buriram restaurants where the locals eat

blocks.html: Food in Buriram is friendly on the wallet, with plenty of long-running spots. We've picked a mix — breakfast joints, noodle shops, grilled chicken, stewed pork leg, and a café — so you can slot them into each day wherever they're convenient.

items.name: Kai Yang Sida
items.blurb: The grilled chicken Buriram locals love, open more than 25 years. The draw is crispy skin over tender, juicy meat — perfect with som tam and sticky rice. On Anuwat Road in town.

items.name: Jay Hung Noodles
items.blurb: The go-to noodle spot in town — fragrant, rich broth and soft, bouncy meatballs. It's what Buriram locals think of when they want noodles for dinner.

items.name: Kwangchow (congee / pork blood soup / red pork rice)
items.blurb: An old-school breakfast and rice-soup shop with congee, pork blood soup, red pork and crispy pork over rice, and wonton noodles — a good way to start the day before heading out.

items.name: Jing Nam Stewed Pork Leg
items.blurb: Pork leg stewed with Chinese herbs, fragrant and fall-apart tender. It's over in Nang Rong district, so it's an easy stop if you're driving south toward Phanom Rung. Open more than 70 years.
items.meta: Stewed pork leg / rice dishes · open around 07:00–20:00

items.name: Kung Jom Prakhon Chai
items.blurb: The punchy local specialty of Prakhon Chai district — fermented small shrimp with a sour-salty kick, eaten with fresh vegetables and fried pork. Worth seeking out when you head down to Mueang Tam.
items.meta: Local cuisine · local Prakhon Chai shops

items.name: Pet Yang Khu Mueang, Buriram branch
items.blurb: A roast duck shop locals recommend — tender duck with rich skin, good over rice or with noodles. An easy, wallet-friendly lunch.

items.name: Baan Chai Nam
items.blurb: A riverside restaurant in town, good for a long, lingering group dinner, with plenty of Thai and Isan dishes to order.

items.name: Home Cafe
items.blurb: A small café tucked down a soi behind Buriram Hospital, with coffee, tea, blended milk drinks, and sweets at friendly prices — a good afternoon rest stop. Closed Mondays.

items: Attraction fees — Phanom Rung 20 THB for Thais, Mueang Tam 20 THB, Khao Kradong free, the Chang Arena tour around 100–150 THB, Pela Plern around 150 THB. Across the whole trip that's roughly 300–350 THB per person for Thais.

Getting around — the sights are spread across several districts, so having your own car or a rental is easiest. Fuel for three days runs about 800–1,200 THB per car. If you don't have a vehicle, hiring a car with a driver by the day is more convenient than connecting songthaews.

Accommodation — hotels in town start in the high hundreds to low thousands of baht. Staying downtown gives you the easiest access to restaurants and Chang Arena. On home-match days or during MotoGP, rooms sell out fast and prices climb, so book ahead.
Souvenirs — Chinese sausage, mu yo, Prakhon Chai kung jom, and local sweets are all easy to find at souvenir shops in town. Buy them on your last day before heading home so they're fresher.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Buriram?
faq.a: If you want to cover the city, the Phanom Rung and Mueang Tam temples, the sports venues, and some nature without rushing, 3 days and 2 nights is just right, because the sights are spread across several districts. One day is enough only if you pick a zone — most people manage just the city plus Khao Kradong, or head south for the temples and nothing else.

faq.q: What are Phanom Rung's hours and entry fee?
faq.a: Open daily 06:00–18:00. Entry is 20 THB for Thais, 100 THB for foreigners, and 30 THB to bring a car in. It's about 77 km from Buriram city, roughly an hour and a half by car. Go in the morning to avoid the heat and the crowds.

faq.q: Can you visit Chang Arena, or do you have to wait for a match day?
faq.a: There's a Stadium Tour you can take even when there's no match, running around 09:00–17:00 for about 100–150 THB. A guide takes you into the players' dressing room, the press room, and down to pitchside. If you're here on a Buriram United home-match day, buying a match ticket gives you fuller atmosphere.

faq.q: Can you visit Buriram without your own car?
faq.a: In the city you can walk and use motorbike taxis, but the standout sights are in outlying districts. Phanom Rung and Pela Plern are far out and public transport isn't convenient, so renting a car or hiring a car with a driver by the day will cover more than relying on songthaews.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Buriram?
faq.a: The cool season, roughly November to February, has the nicest weather, so walking the open-air temples isn't punishing. If you're into sport, late February to early March usually has MotoGP at Chang Circuit, and in April and October there's the phenomenon of the sun shining straight through all 15 doorways at Phanom Rung. All of these draw crowds, though, so book your accommodation ahead.
